summary: Verify “Modified By” user migration from Egnyte to SharePoint Online
description:
In Egnyte, whenever a file or folder is modified, the *Modified By* user is captured.
We need to test whether this *Modified By* user information is correctly migrated when files/folders are migrated from *Egnyte to SharePoint Online (SPO)*.

*Test Scope:*
Egnyte → SharePoint Online migration

*Test Steps:*

# In Egnyte, create a file and a folder using User A.
# Modify the same file/folder using User B.
# Verify the *Modified By* user in Egnyte (Source).
# Migrate the file/folder from Egnyte to SharePoint Online.
# Verify the *Modified By* user in SharePoint Online (Destination).

*Expected Result:*
The *Modified By* user shown in SharePoint Online should match the *Modified By* user from Egnyte.
root_cause: Initiated and validated the migration for the Egnyte to SharePoint Online (SPO) combination on the CNTPOC server to verify the scenario where ‘Created By’ and ‘Modified By’ user metadata for files and folders is accurately migrated.
fix_description: Initiated and validated the migration for the Egnyte to SharePoint Online (SPO) combination on the CNTPOC server to verify the scenario where _‘Created By’_ and _‘Modified By’_ user metadata for files and folders is accurately migrated. The migration was completed successfully, and the user attribution details were preserved as expected

description:
*Description:*
DM’s Stuck in In Queue during Teams to Teams Migration.

*Environment:*
[https://bluerocktech.cloudfuze.com/|https://bluerocktech.cloudfuze.com/|smart-link] 

*Migration Combination:*
Teams to Teams

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Add both Teams (source) and Microsoft Teams (destination) clouds.
# Navigate to Message Migration.
# Select the source and destination clouds.
# Select DM’S for migration.
# Initiate the migration.
# Check DM’s Migration status

*Expected Result:*
The DM’s should move from *In Queue* to *In Progress* and complete the migration successfully.

*Actual Result:*
The DM’s remains stuck in the *In Queue* state and does not proceed further.

*DM’s :* User mentions group dm
*WSID:* 695face17c58e35e5fa6ec66



!image-20260108-134033.png|width=671,alt="image-20260108-134033.png"!
root_cause: The root cause of the issue is many-to-one user mapping during Teams-to-Teams DM migration. When multiple source users are mapped to the same destination user, the system generates a chat creation payload containing duplicate members. Microsoft Graph API enforces strict uniqueness for chat members and rejects the request. Since this failure was not handled correctly, the DM migration process did not update the status and remained stuck in In Queue.
fix_description: The fix ensures that chat members are *deduplicated after user mapping* and before sending the request to Microsoft Graph. Duplicate destination users are filtered out to maintain unique chat participants. Additionally, proper error handling was added so that if chat creation fails, the DM migration status is updated accordingly instead of remaining in *In Queue*. With this fix, DM migrations now move correctly from *In Queue → In Progress → Completed/Failed*.

description:
*Description:*

ELC client has concerns regarding group migration, and this concern is currently a blocker for the migration.

*Groups:* At present, we migrate groups as Microsoft 365 groups by default, which results in the creation of SharePoint sites that are not required.

*Resolution:* To address this, we have proposed creating security groups instead of Microsoft 365 groups. This approach fulfills the required purpose without creating additional, unnecessary SharePoint sites in the environment.

This is something we can achieve by making use of following flag:

We need to enable securityGroupCreation in Clouds collection admin.

*Additionally, the client has another challenge:* there are existing groups in Microsoft 365 with names similar to the Dropbox groups, but with a different set of users.

During group migration, since groups with the same names already exist in the destination, our system uses the existing groups instead of creating new ones. This results in access being granted to users who are not part of the actual team.

*Proposed solution:* To address this issue, we have proposed creating new groups with a specific suffix to clearly differentiate migrated groups from the existing ones.

These newly created groups will be assigned permissions at the folder level, ensuring that access is granted only to the intended users and preventing permissions from being assigned to unrelated users.

*Required action:*

We have already initiated the migration and paused the permissions. After the data migration was completed, we should run the permissions.

For groups, we first fetch the group and create it as a security group with a suffix, as per the user mapping.

We then assign this group at the folder level.
root_cause: Initiated and validated the migration for Dropbox to SharePoint Online (SPO) combination on the QARELEASE server to test the specified scenario involving the creation of security groups in the source (Dropbox). Users were added to these groups and granted both Edit and View permissions.
fix_description: Initiated and validated the migration for *Dropbox* to *SharePoint Online (SPO)* combination on the *QARELEASE* server to test the specified scenario involving the creation of *security groups* in the source (Dropbox). Users were added to these groups and granted both Edit and View permissions. The security groups were successfully migrated to the destination with the expected prefix, _‘_*CloudFuzeQA*_’_. File and folder permissions were accurately preserved during the migration.

root_cause: They raised the ticket because files were not moving. I checked and found that the files were stuck in NOT_PROCESSED.
fix_description:
We checked the respective collections and flags in *FileController*, *ThreadControl*, and the job as well. Then, with the help of a senior, we found the issue: one flag was *disabled at the workspace level*, because of which the movement was stopped. We have enabled it, and now all files have migrated successfully.

Only one file is in *conflict* due to an *omitting partial file exception*; it is *non-retriable*.
